A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAGI, its SAOR and UGDA components, and SAGI-D. Their complete main texts and supplementary Sections 6–9 are readable, and the figures, tables, equations and appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original prompt-generation experiments, a 42-participant human study, forensic-model evaluations, compression tests and demographic analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a comparison of different VLMs within UGDA and a new qualitative UGDA failure case.

M1.justification: SAOR prompt generation, UGDA's two-stage assessment, reversed-image comparisons and classification rule remain unchanged. The new VLM experiment varies a component within the existing procedure; it does not introduce a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use COCO, RAISE and OpenImages, compare against TGIF and CocoGlide, and retain the same manipulation types and compression scenarios. The VLM ablation introduces no reported new dataset, task, population or input environment.

E2.justification: New Table 3 compares GPT-4o-based UGDA with Gemma-3-27B, Mistral-S-3.1-24B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Flash and an explicit no-UGDA baseline. This extends comparisons within one component. The forensic comparator set is unchanged; PSCC and PSCC-Net denote the same method.

E3.justification: The added VLM evaluation varies backbone configurations, including 7B, 24B and 27B models, and compares filtered images with an unfiltered control using human accuracy and IoU. Existing experiments retain their reported splits, training arrangements and metrics. Newly stated preprocessing details do not establish changed preprocessing.

E4.justification: v3 adds a systematic six-VLM ablation directly examining UGDA's dependence on its foundation model, substantially extending validation of this central component. It also adds an explicit order-dependent UGDA failure analysis. The balloon failure redisplayed in Figure 3 already appeared in v2's supplementary Figure 9.

E5.justification: Both report 3–5 human assessments per image and the same demographic chi-square tests, Cramer's V values and p-values in v2 Table 12/v3 Table 13. v3 introduces no additional seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports human accuracy/IoU of 54.9/26.4 without UGDA and 35.2/12.7 with GPT-4o, plus results for five alternative VLMs. Table 2 reverses the deceiving/non-deceiving IoU entries from 39.9/12.7 to 12.7/39.9, correcting their group assignment rather than demonstrating a performance improvement. Other matched numerical tables and compression plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, the semantic-distribution formulation, UGDA classification rule and assumption about stability under semantically invariant perturbations retain their mathematical content. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The model-agnostic framework, SAOR/UGDA contributions, dataset-scale claims and headline human and forensic performance claims retain their scope. The new VLM ablation supports the existing model-agnostic claim rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: The new failure discussion explains how fixation on couch duplication can make UGDA overlook blur and connects this behavior to foundation-model biases. The conclusion replaces proposed human-in-the-loop refinement with possible extensions to reference-based image translation, audio/video editing and generated-content assessment.

D1.justification: v3 newly states that original padding and normalization strategies are retained, corrects the Stable Diffusion v2 checkpoint link, and provides a project-page access link while retaining the repository link in the appendix. It omits v2's statement that cross-dataset test sets were modified to avoid leakage; this is a disclosure change, not evidence that leakage controls were removed.

R1.justification: Five VLM sources are added for the new ablation, while the MUSIQ and Kramer autoencoder references and associated survey mentions are removed. The positioning against existing inpainting datasets and realism-assessment approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Extensive paragraph-level editing condenses and rewrites the introduction, related work, method explanations and results discussion. Terminology changes include 'undeceiving' to 'non-deceiving' and expanded PSCC-Net naming, alongside revised appendix headings. These edits extend well beyond accommodating the new scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adds the VLM-ablation Table 3 and failure-case Figure 3, combining the existing balloon example with a new couch pair. Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 5, and several captions and labels are revised. Existing graphics and supplementary displays otherwise remain, with subsequent renumbering.

improvement.justification: The VLM ablation strengthens evidence for UGDA's model independence, and the couch example makes a failure mechanism explicit. Correcting Table 2's reversed IoUs also restores consistency with the appendix's finding that deceiving images are harder to localize. These provide limited net gains in validation and clarity, tempered by sparse setup details for the new ablation and omission of the earlier leakage-control note.
